Q: How to retrieve argv and argc in assembly language for x86_64 processors on Linux (SYSTEM V) OS A:

TL;DR

The revised/improved example code can be found in the The improved example code section below.

Explanation & tutorial

The argc/argv are pushed on stack by OS, so your assembly code needs to pop them out from stack into registers in order to use them. There's a tutorial about it with detailed diagram of stack layout as well as demo code to show the command line arguments using just assembly code. See the document/tutorial from this GitHub repo:

https://github.com/LilSuperUser/x86_64-asm-tutorials/blob/main/notes/013-CLI_arguments.md

Note that the example assembly code shown in the tutorial is written in nasm format/flavor. In order to use it, you will need to install "nasm". On Debian distro (or all those derived from Debian), you can install it with this command:

sudo apt install nasm

To generate the executable:

nasm -f elf64 sample.s -o sample.o
ld sample.o -o sample

For other distros, the install command would be different but you probably knew how already. If your assembler is not "nasm", you should translate it to the proper syntax, but it shouldn't be hard.

The improved example code

Stack Overflow encourages showing actual code embedded inside the question/answer instead of external link because the content referenced by external link might disappear someday. The original demo code is from LilSuperUser but it contains multiple bugs when the argc is greater than a digit can hold and the output contains invisible characters. There are also memory alignment issues, too. A revised version is thus shown below. Thanks to Peter Cordes's suggestions to fix the bugs.

The key instructions for popping argc/argv from the stack are written in capital POP to draw your attention. Their comments also start with *** as well.

%macro writeStdout 2             ; writeStdout(const char* str, size_t str_len)
    mov rax, 1                   ; sys_write
    mov rdi, 1                   ; stdout
    %ifidni rsi, %1              ; set rsi only if %1 is not rsi
    %else
        mov rsi, %1              ; pointer to string
    %endif
    %ifidni edx, %2              ; set edx only if %2 is not edx
    %else
        mov edx, %2              ; str_len
    %endif
    syscall
%endmacro

%macro print 1                   ; short-hand to print inline string, string data is saved in .data section
    section .data
        %%str     db  %1
        %%str_len equ $ - %%str
    section .text
        writeStdout %%str, %%str_len
%endmacro

newline equ 10                   ; ASCII code for new-line

section .text
    global _start

_start:
    print "Number of arguments are: "
    POP   r15                    ; *** pop the stack into r15 which is argc provided by OS
    mov   rdi, r15               ; call subroutine to print argc, which uses rdi as input
    call  printNumber            ; ...
    print newline

    xor   rbx, rbx               ; clear rbx to use it as a counter
.printArgsLoop:                  ; start of the arguments loop
        cmp   rbx, r15           ; compare the value of rbx with argc
        jge   .printArgsDone     ; if rbx >= value in 'argc', break the loop
        inc   rbx                ; if rbx < *argc, increment rbx by 1
        print "Argument number "
        mov   rdi, rbx           ; call subroutine to print the counter
        call  printNumber        ; ...
        print " is: "
        POP   rsi                ; *** pop the stack into rsi so it now contains the next C-string argument

        mov   rdi, rsi           ; prepare destination pointer rdi for scasb, points at start of C-string
        mov   rcx, -1            ; set rcx to "infinite" count
        xor   eax, eax           ; set search target (AL) to <NUL>
        repne scasb              ; start searching until <NUL> is found
        not   rcx                ; invert the bits, result is length + 1
        dec   rcx                ; subtract the count on <NUL> and save to rcx

        writeStdout rsi, ecx     ; rsi now contains the address of argv[i], ecx contains its length (not counting <NUL>)
        print newline
        jmp   .printArgsLoop     ; end of loop

.printArgsDone:
    mov rax, 60                  ; load 60 into rax (SYS_exit)
    xor edi, edi                 ; load 0 into edi (exit code)
    syscall                      ; invoke the syscall

;------------------------------------------------------------
; printNumber
; Input:  rdi = unsigned integer to print
; Uses:   digits buffer is kept in stack (20 bytes)
;------------------------------------------------------------
    digits_buf_size equ  20      ; enough decimal digits to print maximum value in rdi

printNumber:
    sub rsp, digits_buf_size     ; reserve enough space for digits buffer
    mov rsi, rsp                 ; rsi points to start of the buffer
    add rsi, digits_buf_size     ; rsi now just past the end of buffer
    xor ecx, ecx                 ; clear digits counter
    mov r10, 10                  ; prepare divisor: 10

.printNumberLoop:
        dec rsi                  ; step back one byte
        inc ecx                  ; increment digits counter by 1
        cmp rdi, r10
        jl .printNumberLastDigit ; if < 10, this should be the last digit

        xor edx, edx             ; clear previous remainder, if any
        mov rax, rdi             ; prepare dividend
        div r10                  ; division by 10 output: rax = quotient, edx = remainder (range 0~9)
        add dl, '0'              ; add remainder ASCII code '0'
        mov [rsi], dl            ; store the decimal digit to buffer
        mov rdi, rax             ; quotient becomes the new current number
        jmp .printNumberLoop

.printNumberLastDigit:
    add dil, '0'                 ; convert the digit, add ASCII code '0'
    mov [rsi], dil               ; store it

    writeStdout rsi, ecx         ; rsi now points at first digit, ecx contains digits count
    add rsp, digits_buf_size     ; restore stack space (discard digits buffer)
    ret

Finally, Theo de Raadt adds a getexecpath function in libc to get a realpath-like qualified copy of the ELF program's execution path => commit here https://github.com/openbsd/src/commit/026846f111232f45cd1f4883414c190c8ff722a7

Q: How to get Hugo warnings to appear in RStudio console using blogdown A:

Someone had given an answer that solved my issue, but I now see this answer has disappeared, so I'll write it myself.

I added blogdown.server.verbose = TRUE to options() in my .Rprofile file and it works perfectly. I now get all the Hugo output in the R console, including the warnings.

Q: Connect to ftps:// URL A:

The ftps:// prefix is not a standard IANA URI scheme. There's only ftp:// scheme, as defined by RFC 1738.

Anyway, the ftps:// is still recognized by some software to refer to an FTP over TLS/SSL protocol (secure FTP). This mimics https:// scheme, which is an HTTP over TLS/SSL (https:// is a standard scheme).

Though the ftps:// is NOT recognized by the .NET framework.

To connect to the explicit mode FTP over TLS/SSL, change your URI to ftp://, and set FtpWebRequest.EnableSsl to true (what you are doing already).

Note that the ftps:// prefix commonly refers to an implicit mode FTP over TLS/SSL. The .NET framework supports only an explicit mode. Though even if your URI is indeed referring to the implicit mode, most servers would support the explicit mode too anyway. So this won't be a problem typically. For the explicit mode, ftpes:// is sometimes used. See my article to understand the difference between FTP over TLS/SSL implicit and explicit modes.

Q: Custom Chinese font Noto Sans SC is not being used in Flutter A:

theme and darkTheme are two separate ThemeData objects. With ThemeMode.system, Flutter selects darkTheme when the system is using dark mode; it does not inherit fontFamily from theme.

Set the font on the dark theme as well:

return MaterialApp(
  title: 'Did App',
  theme: ThemeData(
    colorScheme: lightColorScheme,
    useMaterial3: true,
    fontFamily: 'NotoSansSC',
  ),
  darkTheme: ThemeData(
    colorScheme: darkColorScheme,
    useMaterial3: true,
    fontFamily: 'NotoSansSC',
  ),
  themeMode: ThemeMode.system,
  home: const MyHomePage(title: 'Did App'),
);

Also make sure that the font declaration is nested under the top-level flutter key:

flutter:
  fonts:
    - family: NotoSansSC
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/font.ttf

A minimal widget test reproduces the theme issue: in dark system mode the active text style does not use NotoSansSC until fontFamily is set on darkTheme itself.

If the font is still wrong in both light and dark modes, check that font.ttf actually contains the required Chinese glyphs and do a full restart after changing the asset declaration; otherwise Flutter may use a fallback font.

References: MaterialApp.themeMode, Flutter custom fonts.

Q: Implement SCD2 logic in Data Fusion and BigQuery A:

For SCD2 in Data Fusion, the BigQuery sink does support Insert/Update/Upsert via its "Operation" field plus a "Table Key", which generates a MERGE under the hood. But that's not enough for a real SCD2 because you need to close the old row and insert a new one in the same shot.

The clean solution is to land your stage data into a BigQuery staging table with a normal sink, then add a BigQuery Execute action as a post-step of the pipeline, where you write your full SCD2 MERGE (WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE end_date / is_current, WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT). You can almost copy paste the SQL from the Medium article.

That's the most maintenable way, and it gives you the atomicity a split-stream approach would not.
